summary: self_organize.py lines 7900-9859 are the end-of-run report battery inside main(): ~30 printed sections plus the final `_config_audit()`. It opens with a final re-tokenisation sanity pass and `_save_ckpt`, then runs the held-out battery (MEMORIZATION CHECK + ANCHORS, ACROSS THE RUN BOUNDARY via `report_holdout`, RETENTION, LEARNING CURVE, CAN A DOMAIN PREDICT, WORLD MODEL), the LM-curve verdict cascade, the fabric/domain structural sections (CHAINING, POPULATION CHURN, DID IT FIRE, domain genuineness), then the memory sections (WRONGNESS, PERFORMANCE / CROSS-SEGMENT COMPOSITION / IS THE PARTITION INFORMATIVE — all three live in `compose_test` at 3715-3846 and are printed from the call at 8949), then the expert sections (AFFILIATION, EXPERT INDEPENDENCE, FABRIC, SIGNATURE SPACE, SPECIALIZATION/ROUTER SELECTION/CHAIN ORDER/SUFFICIENCY), then GENERATION, IS IT COMPOSING, COHERENCE, NON-STATIONARY and the UNLEARN edits. The samples split three ways and the headings mostly do not say which: the held-out tail `VALC` (memorization, anchors, boundary probe, learning curve, domain-prior), the TRAINING stream `stream` via `eval_win` (retention, fabric ablation, expert independence, specialization, non-stationary, unlearn, compose_test), and report-time probes that call a forward path the run may never have trained (the fabric mass/depth probe, SUFFICIENCY's `fab.society` call). Almost every section is individually wrapped in try/except so a broken instrument degrades to a one-line skip.

facts.claim: RETENTION conditions on the process label and compares each process's earliest windows against its latest (k = min(48, len(_at)//3), requires >=32 windows), so both ends are the same material.

RETENTION's verdict is taken over the WORST drift among processes that existed before this run (`_old_names = set(_hb or {})`), and falls back to all processes with an explicit 'this is acquisition, not retention' caveat when no process predates the run.
RETENTION's drift is `latest - earliest` (positive = forgetting), matching the sentence printed below it; the docstring records that the subtraction used to be reversed.

LEARNING CURVE is computed from `_CURVE`, which is sampled on the RATE_EVERY cadence on HELD-OUT text (16 fixed windows per domain from VALC), so it is a different sample from RETENTION printed immediately above it; the section heading does not say held-out.
facts.evidence: self_organize.py:6385 `if RATE_EVERY and step % RATE_EVERY == 0 and step > _s_mark and VALC:`; :6396-6413; :8111 heading

facts.claim: LEARNING CURVE splits consecutive-probe deltas by the was-ACTIVE flag: deltas measured while active are summed into acquisition, while absent into decay, and the ABSENT column is empty unless PHASED fills it.

CAN A DOMAIN PREDICT is on held-out text, needs >=16 collected windows and draws min(48, EVAL_N) per domain; below 16 it prints an explicit NOT RUN line naming DOM_PRIOR as paid-for-and-unread rather than falling silent.

CAN A DOMAIN PREDICT assigns each held-out window to a domain by encoding a WIN-length BYTE window of the raw validation text and taking the nearest `asm.cent` centroid, i.e. the assembler's own rule, and the random arm is guaranteed to be a different domain.

The whole block from MEMORIZATION CHECK through CAN A DOMAIN PREDICT is inside one try; `_NoHeldOut` is raised deliberately when VALC is empty so a configuration that cannot support the battery is distinguishable from a genuine failure, and the message says BWT/F are skipped with it.
WORLD MODEL is evaluated on held-out VALC windows against a persistence baseline (`F.mse_loss(_zt, _zn)`) plus a latent-std collapse check; the verdict requires positive beat AND std > ~0.5.

`[LM training curve]` is the trailing-2000-step mean of the pure LM cross-entropy on the TRAINING stream (per TOKEN), not the composite objective — `loss` is `_plw.mean()` and the auxiliary terms are added into `tot` afterwards.
The unit-stable cross-check for the LM curve uses `_curve_by_step(_CURVE)`, which averages only rows whose was-ACTIVE flag is set, falling back to all rows when nothing is marked active.
facts.evidence: self_organize.py:8256-8260; :879-892 `rows = [(st, b) for st, _p, b, _a in curve if _a] or [...]`

facts.claim: `curve_verdict` is a pure function of three numbers with five module-level thresholds (CURVE_RISE_BLEWUP=0.5, CURVE_FLAT=0.05, CURVE_TOK_RISE=0.05) and has a companion test file, curve_test.py.
'SELF-ASSEMBLED N LIVE domains' counts `len(asm.cent)` and reports recurrence as entries per live domain against DOM_MIN_VISITS.

CHAINING prints no measurement of its own except the training HALT mass; it is a prose description of which forward path SOCIETY selected, and it states outright that on SOCIETY=1 the DEPTH figure below is a report-time probe of a path the run did not use.

POPULATION CHURN's growth-reason counts are per-run deltas (`getattr(fabgrow,k) - _fg_base[k]`) and are explicitly documented as counting TRIGGERS, with a separate `declined_why` line for events that produced no expert.

DID IT FIRE builds every row through `_r(name, get_n, get_armed, why)` with each lambda individually try/except'd, so a broken row degrades to '?' and the rest still print; config is read through `_cfg`, which reads `_SPEC` rather than restating defaults.

The DID IT FIRE print loop drops the counter entirely for any row whose armed test is False — it prints `off <name> -- <why>` with no number — so a mechanism that fired but whose arming test says it could not have shows no count.
DID IT FIRE runs BEFORE the WRONGNESS section that calls `selfcheck()`, which is the only caller of selfcheck in the file; the report says so in prose in the wrongness section.

A live domain with an empty reservoir is skipped (`continue`) but still counts in the denominator of the printed '{genuine}/{len(live)} live domains GENUINE'.

facts.claim: PERFORMANCE, CROSS-SEGMENT COMPOSITION and IS THE PARTITION INFORMATIVE are all printed from `compose_test`, whose windows come from the TRAINING stream; PERFORMANCE says so in its own body and cross-references the held-out pair carried in `_HELDOUT_MEM`.

`compose_test` computes its base distribution as `F.softmax(model(X)[0], -1)` — the bare LM head, with no fabric — so on a FABRIC run the PERFORMANCE, CROSS-SEGMENT and PARTITION numbers describe a model path that is not the one `_eval_logits` uses everywhere else.

facts.claim: IS THE PARTITION INFORMATIVE compares own-domain against a random-other-domain retrieval at matched restriction and subtracts a shuffled-provenance null averaged over INFO_NULLS=5 permutations, with the verdict at 2 sigma of the null spread.

AFFILIATION reads `dom_exp`, accumulated during training, resolves merged domains through `asm.resolve` and keeps only live ones; an expert 'serves' a domain at AFF_MIN=0.10 share, and the blast-radius rows are the 5 domains with the most accumulated mass.

EXPERT INDEPENDENCE picks the busiest expert from a SINGLE probe window (`stream[:WIN]` paired with a signature from `ENC_SEQ[WIN*3:WIN*4]`), deletes it, re-scores every process on the same fixed eval windows, and prints mean collateral against a hard |0.3| threshold.

The FABRIC section's node-mass probe pairs token windows `stream[q:q+WIN]` with signature windows read at the SAME index into ENC_SEQ, without going through `encpos()`, which is the function that exists to convert a token index to an ENC_SEQ index.

The FABRIC section prints an explicit caveat that 'model ALONE' is an ablation of a component the model trained with (it also removes the fabric's LayerNorm) and names the honest cross-run comparison instead.
SIGNATURE SPACE encodes up to 200 windows taken from the FIRST 200*WIN positions of the TRAINING stream and prints them as 'held-back windows'.
facts.evidence: self_organize.py:9093 `_sw2 = [encwin(encpos(a)) for a in range(0, min(len(stream) - WIN - 2, 200 * WIN), WIN)][:200]`; :9104 `{len(_sw2)} held-back windows`

facts.claim: SIGNATURE SPACE's DEGENERATE verdict fires on `mean pairwise cosine distance < 0.10 OR participation ratio < 2.0`, both of which are printed on the line above it.

SPECIALIZATION partitions windows using the router that actually ran — `fab.entry_logits` when `fab.grounded`, falling back to the old `q_entry` expression otherwise — and the comment records that the un-updated q_entry copy made every earlier INTERCHANGEABLE verdict void.

SPECIALIZATION's per-node bits/byte `_bw` is the FULL population prediction (`fab_logits`) on each window, grouped by which node won the window at entry — not that node's own prediction. The shuffled null therefore tests whether entry-winner identity groups windows of differing difficulty.

ROUTER SELECTION reads `fab.use`, which counts TRAINING top-1 wins only (both bump_use sites are gated on learn_regions), and is compared to the probe's winners by MEMBERSHIP plus a coupon-collector coverage null, after an earlier version's units-mismatched `len(_used)*10 < len(_uv)` guard was removed as unsatisfiable.
GRADIENT REACH reports the mean of `_greach`, sampled on a cadence during training, as 'experts that received a nonzero gradient on a typical step'.

CHAIN ORDER computes H(hop1|hop0) from `fab._ord`, gated to the non-SOCIETY path with an explicit note that on the society path forward() only runs in the report probe and would report a 1-sample artifact.

SUFFICIENCY calls `fab.society(...)` unconditionally, including on the default SOCIETY=0 chaining run, so the 'population blended' and 'best single rank-slot' figures come from a forward path the default run never trained.
facts.evidence: self_organize.py:9487-9489 `_ws, _Os, _os = fab.society(_hs, _G, torch.zeros(...), k=max(ENS_K, 2), learn_regions=False)`; contrast :8385-8388 which describes society() as the non-default path

facts.claim: The EXPERTS (adapters) section only runs when EXPERTS is on and separates PINNED (the expert the span trained with, via `route_at`) from ROUTED (nearest centroid at eval), which is the routing-mismatch cost.
GENERATION samples from the FINAL model and prints an explicit note that the final model is typically worse than the best, naming the best step and whether it was saved.

IS IT COMPOSING measures 'generated words that appear in the training text' against a vocabulary built from the FIRST corpus only (`CORP[:1]`, first 4 MB), while the generated words are pooled across every sampled process.
IS IT COMPOSING pools only the MODEL-ONLY generations into `_gw`; the model+memory continuations are collected in `_gen_keep` and never scored.

facts.claim: COHERENCE draws its OWN sample (COH_N=16 seeds x COH_LEN=384 tokens), prints a standard error and an explicit 'inside the noise' clause, and brackets the score with a real-text ceiling and a 1/len(_cent) chance floor.

COHERENCE falls back to the SELF-ASSEMBLED domains as the reference when fewer than two true-corpus centroids exist, labels that as weaker evidence in the printed output, and measures the seed's home domain by encoding the seed rather than by looking up a label.

NON-STATIONARY runs only under PHASED, scores ACTIVE vs FADED processes on the TRAINING stream via `bpb_true` (memory ON by default), and reports surviving memory entries per process by mapping mem.src through `s2t`.

The per-process surviving-memory line silently drops any memory whose source domain is not a key of `s2t` (a domain with no window in `assigns`, or the injected src=99), so the printed counts need not sum to the active store.

The UNLEARN edits are destructive and sequential: `_edit_test` deletes an ACTIVE process's domains, then a FADED one's, then the final whole-process UNLEARN deletes another; each later test measures on a store already stripped by the earlier ones.
The two unlearn tests use different LOCAL/LEAKED thresholds for the same word: 0.1 in `_edit_test` and 0.05 in the final UNLEARN.
facts.evidence: self_organize.py:9839 `{'LOCAL' if abs(_dl) < 0.1 else 'LEAKED'}`; :9852 `{'LOCAL' if abs(ao-bo) < 0.05 else 'LEAKED'}`

facts.claim: The final UNLEARN target is the true process with the most SELF-DOMAINS, not the most windows or the most memory entries.
facts.evidence: self_organize.py:9843 `tgt = Counter([s2t[d] for d in by]).most_common(1)[0][0]`

facts.claim: clustering reports purity, homogeneity, completeness and V-measure together with the fragmentation ratio, and the code comments record that reporting purity alone read 0.96 on a 96-domain partition of 4 corpora.
RECURRENCE counts a 'visit' as a maximal run of consecutive windows assigned to the same domain and calls artifacts dominant when >50% of domains are visited once.

The final `_save_ckpt(stream)` at the top of the report writes a fresh `holdout` probe into the checkpoint, so the baseline the NEXT run compares against is computed before any of the report's destructive edits.

`LOSS_MASK_DEAD` defaults to 0, so `mask_dead` is an identity on the default configuration and the masked/unmasked asymmetry between `fab_logits` and bare `model.head` paths has no numeric effect unless the knob is turned on.
facts.evidence: self_organize.py:669 `LOSS_MASK_DEAD = bool(_i("LOSS_MASK_DEAD", 0))`; :3973 `if not (LOSS_MASK_DEAD and USE_TOK and TOK is not None): return lg`

levers.name: EVAL_N
levers.effect: Sets four different sample sizes in the report: the memorization check caps at min(24, EVAL_N) windows/domain, CAN A DOMAIN PREDICT draws min(48, EVAL_N)/domain and needs 16 total or it does not run, `eval_win` (the fixed per-process window set for independence/fabric/experts/non-stationary/unlearn) is EVAL_N/process, compose_test draws EVAL_N/process, and the fabric mass probe uses min(EVAL_N, ...) windows.
levers.owner: the report battery in main() (7942-9856) plus compose_test

levers.name: HOLDOUT_N
levers.effect: Windows per domain in `holdout_bpb`, which produces ACROSS THE RUN BOUNDARY, the memory decomposition, BWT, F and the checkpoint's stored baseline. Independent of EVAL_N, so the two 'held-out bits/byte' figures in the report are different samples.
levers.evidence: self_organize.py:5088 `range(_i("HOLDOUT_N", 32))`; :9553-9558 the note that the two disagree by up to 0.190

levers.name: DOM_PRIOR
levers.effect: Both the gate for the CAN A DOMAIN PREDICT section (`if DOM_PRIOR > 0.0 and asm.tokc and len(asm.cent) >= 2 and VALC`) and the blend weight used in its four arms. At 0 the per-window asm.tokc histogram is still accumulated during training but never read.
levers.owner: the CAN A DOMAIN PREDICT block (8146-8205)

levers.name: GENUINE_MIN / GENUINE_SIL
levers.effect: The two conjuncts of the GENUINE verdict: size >= GENUINE_MIN AND silhouette >= GENUINE_SIL. Sizes come from asm.size (per-window, incremented in update()), not from the report's own `by` counts.

levers.name: WRONG_CHECK / WRONG_INJECT / WRONG_SWEEP
levers.effect: WRONG_CHECK gates the whole wrongness block. WRONG_INJECT is the number of synthetic cross-domain entries written with src=99 (bypassing the write gate) to give precision/recall a positive class. WRONG_SWEEP=1 takes the sweep branch — which is also the branch that does NOT delete the injected entries or clear selfcon before the rest of the report runs.

levers.name: MEM_WRONG_READ
levers.effect: Whether the wrongness flag gates retrieval in Memory.read. In the report it also zeroes the '_nblk excluded from EVERY retrieval' figure when off, and is one of the two conjuncts arming the memory.wrong_block DID IT FIRE row.

levers.name: EXPERT_NULLS
levers.effect: Number of assignment shuffles used as the null for SPECIALIZATION; the verdict is `_spread > _nm + 2*_nsd`, so this knob sets the resolution of the only thing standing between SPECIALIZED and INTERCHANGEABLE.

levers.name: INFO_NULLS
levers.effect: Number of provenance permutations forming the floor for IS THE PARTITION INFORMATIVE; the verdict is `excess > 2*sd + 1e-9`, and the comment records two identical runs printing opposite conclusions when this was 1.

levers.name: COH_N / COH_LEN
levers.effect: Sample size and continuation length for COHERENCE. The section explicitly exists because scoring the GEN_PROCS printed samples gave a four-sample mean with SE 0.25.

levers.name: GEN_N / GEN_PROCS / GEN_LEN / GEN_TEMP / GENERATE
levers.effect: Number of distinct seed passages per process, number of processes sampled, continuation length and sampling temperature for the printed generations; GENERATE gates the whole generation/composing/coherence group.

levers.name: AFF_MIN
levers.effect: Share threshold at which an expert counts as 'serving' a domain; drives the exclusive/shared/idle counts, the domains-per-expert histogram and the blast-radius orphan counts.

levers.name: ENS_K
levers.effect: Number of experts blended in SUFFICIENCY's population arm (`k=max(ENS_K, 2)`), so it sets both the 'population' figure and how many rank slots the best-single-member baseline is minimised over.

levers.name: SIG_WIN
levers.effect: Declared as the signature window width (0 = derive it from the vocabulary in `_sigwidth`), but `_eval_sig` uses it as a raw length via `[-max(1, SIG_WIN):]`, so at the default 0 every eval-path signature is one byte long.
levers.owner: _sigwidth() (5675-5680) should own it; _eval_sig (3907-3927) reads it directly

levers.name: EVAL_GIST
levers.effect: 1 = eval windows get a real signature from `_eval_sig`; 0 = every eval call falls back to the all-zero placeholder gist, which ranks the population identically for every window.

levers.name: FAB_N0
levers.effect: Read at report time as the baseline for POPULATION CHURN's net-growth figure and for the FABRIC one-liner's 'grown on plateau from N'. It is the environment value, not the population size this run actually started at.

levers.name: PHASED
levers.effect: Gates the entire NON-STATIONARY section and both `_edit_test` unlearn probes; also changes what RETENTION means (it adds a caveat line when PHASED=0 saying retention is easy by construction) and whether the LEARNING CURVE's ABSENT column can be non-empty.

levers.name: RATE_EVERY
levers.effect: Cadence of the held-out per-process probe that fills `_CURVE`; the LEARNING CURVE prints its acquisition/decay rates per RATE_EVERY steps, and `_curve_by_step` (the unit-stable cross-check for the LM curve) is built from the same series.

levers.name: BEST_TRACK / BEST_KEEP / BEST_KEEP_TOL / SAVE_CKPT
levers.effect: Gate the 'SAMPLED FROM: the FINAL model, not the best' block, the rotating BEST-KEEP slot listing and the 'to sample the BEST model' hint; with SAVE_CKPT off every save returns False and the report says 'not saved' rather than printing a path.

levers.name: GROW_CAP / GROW_CAP_FAB / GROW_CAP_VOCAB / GROW_CAP_EVERY / GROW_CAP_PLATEAU / PLATEAU_WARM
levers.effect: Gate and parameterise the CAPACITY VALVE report, which distinguishes never-reached-cap, reached-but-not-held, earned-but-plateau-test-never-ran, and earned-but-never-flat using the high-water marks in `_pin_seen` and `_plat_seen`.

bugs.title: Every eval-path signature is built from ONE BYTE: `_eval_sig` uses SIG_WIN raw, whose default 0 becomes max(1,0)=1
bugs.symptom: On the default config (SIG_SPACE=bytes, TOKENIZER=1, SIG_WIN unset), `_eval_sig` decodes each eval window back to bytes and then keeps only the last `max(1, SIG_WIN)` = 1 byte before encoding it. Every held-out and retention figure that goes through `_eval_logits` therefore routes the fabric on a signature derived from a single byte of context, while training routed on a `_sigw`-byte window (`_sigwidth()` returns max(WIN, WIN*bytes_per_token) when SIG_WIN==0). The router is not blind — the zero-gist fallback that `_eval_sig` was written to replace — but it is near-blind, and nothing in the report says so. Affected: MEMORIZATION CHECK (train and held-out), ANCHORS' THIS MODEL, RETENTION, LEARNING CURVE / `_CURVE`, `holdout_bpb` and hence ACROSS THE RUN BOUNDARY / BWT / F / the checkpoint's stored baseline, and CAN A DOMAIN PREDICT's model term.
bugs.evidence: `_w = [list(TOK.decode(r.tolist()).encode("utf-8", "replace"))[-max(1, SIG_WIN):] or [0] for r in x]` (self_organize.py:3919); `SIG_WIN = _i("SIG_WIN", 0)` (:3136); registry default `"SIG_WIN": ("i", 0)` (:351); `def _sigwidth(): if SIG_WIN > 0: return SIG_WIN; ... return max(WIN, int(WIN * max(1.0, _b)))` (:5675-5679) shows 0 means 'derive', not 'one'.

bugs.title: The LM-curve verdict cascade prints 'still improving or flat' immediately after BLEW UP / PLATEAUED / RECOVERED / NOT DIVERGING
bugs.symptom: The bits/byte verdict block (`if _bpb_dir is not None:` at 8290) prints one of vocab / blewup / recovering / plateau. The NEXT statement is an independent if/elif/else: the `if` only fires on 'diverging', the `elif` requires `_bpb_dir is None`, so whenever `_bpb_dir` exists and the verdict is anything but 'diverging' the `else` fires and prints '>> still improving or flat: falling = more passes/steps will help; flat = the model has converged...'. A run told 'BLEW UP AND STAYED DOWN... something broke, the run never recovered it' is told two lines later that it is still improving or flat and needs more capacity or data.

carry_forward.item: There are TWO 'held-out bits/byte' instruments and they are not the same measurement: the MEMORIZATION CHECK's mean over <=min(24,EVAL_N) random windows per corpus, and the learning-curve/holdout probe over HOLDOUT_N windows seeded per domain NAME. Across 36 logs they disagreed in 27 by more than 0.03 and by up to 0.190, sign going both ways.
carry_forward.why: 0.190 is larger than most arm effects this project has claimed; quoting one as the other silently invalidates comparisons.
carry_forward.evidence: self_organize.py:9553-9558 (the note printed in GENERATION); :7958 vs :5088

carry_forward.item: Three different signature window widths coexist: the contrastive encoder is TRAINED on WIN-byte windows, the assembler/router uses `_sigw` = max(WIN, WIN*bytes_per_token) bytes during training, the report's `encwin()` uses WIN bytes, and `_eval_sig` uses `max(1, SIG_WIN)` = 1 byte by default. Any rebuild must pick one and route every site through it.
carry_forward.why: Centroids are means of encoded windows, so signatures taken at different widths are not comparable — the file already documents that a width that MOVES mid-run is wrong in principle; a width that differs between training and the report has the same defect.

carry_forward.item: `Fabric.remove` is a swap-with-last that mutates ten per-expert dicts, not just the five parameter tensors. Any code that removes an expert temporarily must restore `use, uage, born, ef, es, births, comp, contrib, dom_of, rescued` or accept that every later expert diagnostic is reading a permuted mapping.
carry_forward.why: The EXPERT INDEPENDENCE ablation currently restores only the tensors and then prints 'expert restored ... the INTACT model', and four later sections read the corrupted dicts.

carry_forward.item: An armed test that reads a SNAPSHOT (`cull_ran`, `n_elig`) against a CUMULATIVE counter is the DID IT FIRE audit's own recurring bug. The rows that were fixed (tokenizer.mint, lr.restart) all OR in 'or the count is nonzero'; fabric.rescue and fabric.cull_eligible still do not.
carry_forward.why: An unarmed row prints no number at all, so the disagreement between the arming test and the count — which is itself the finding — is thrown away.

carry_forward.item: `compose_test` scores through the bare `model(X)[0]` head, not through `_eval_logits`/`fab_logits`. On a FABRIC run its PERFORMANCE, CROSS-SEGMENT COMPOSITION and PARTITION INFORMATIVENESS numbers describe a different model than every other section.
carry_forward.why: `_eval_logits` exists specifically as 'the one line that must never drift between the six evaluation sites'; compose_test is a seventh site that never adopted it.

carry_forward.item: `_curve_by_step` filters the per-process curve to ACTIVE rows because an absent process's rise is the phase schedule, not divergence (2.51 -> 4.64 recorded). Any new consumer of `_CURVE` must apply the same filter; the GENERATION preamble currently does not.
carry_forward.why: Feeding absent-process rows to a divergence or best-vs-final comparison answers a question about the schedule while claiming to answer one about the model.

carry_forward.item: Almost every report section is wrapped in its own try/except that prints a one-line skip. That is deliberate — a diagnostic must not end a run that has already trained and checkpointed — but it means a section vanishing is a signal, and the DID IT FIRE audit and the expert-specialization block additionally print a traceback because a bare message could not locate the fault.
carry_forward.why: Several past failures (a NameError on _hb, an AttributeError on fab.keys, an int() of a whole row in SUFFICIENCY) removed entire sections from the report for many runs with only a one-line note.

carry_forward.item: The final `_save_ckpt(stream)` runs BEFORE the report, and the checkpoint's `holdout` field is a fresh `holdout_bpb()` call. Keep that ordering: everything after it (wrongness injection, delete_src, the unlearn edits) mutates the memory store destructively.
carry_forward.why: If the save moved below the report, the next run's cross-boundary baseline would be measured on a store the report had already deleted two processes from.

carry_forward.item: Section verdict thresholds are hardcoded and inconsistent across sections that use the same words: LOCAL is |delta|<0.1 in `_edit_test` and <0.05 in the final UNLEARN; INDEPENDENT is |mean collateral|<0.3; DOMAINS PREDICT needs both gaps >0.01; SPECIALIZED needs >2 sigma of an EXPERT_NULLS-sized shuffle; PARTITION INFORMATIVE needs >2 sigma of an INFO_NULLS-sized permutation; RETAINED/DRIFTING/CATASTROPHIC at 0.10/0.40.
carry_forward.why: Two sections can print opposite-sounding verdicts about comparable effect sizes purely because of which threshold they inherited.

carry_forward.item: `_HELDOUT_MEM` is the only channel by which the held-out with/without-memory pair reaches the PERFORMANCE section; it is filled by `_decompose` inside `report_holdout` and read 5200 lines later in `compose_test`. If report_holdout is skipped (no held-out data, or an exception before it), PERFORMANCE correctly prints the 'no held-out comparison was produced' branch.
carry_forward.why: A module-level dict is the coupling between two sections that answer the same question on different text and print 127 lines apart; breaking it silently reverts PERFORMANCE to being a memorisation score with no counterweight.

open_questions: Is `_eval_sig`'s `max(1, SIG_WIN)` intended to be `_sigw` (the assembler's derived width) or WIN? `_sigw` is a main() local and `_eval_sig` is module-level, which is the same visibility problem `_ENC` was introduced to solve — so the fix may need a second holder. I could not find any run log in the repo to confirm what the one-byte signature does to the held-out numbers empirically.

Does the report's `enc(...)` on raw BYTE windows (CAN A DOMAIN PREDICT at 8168, COHERENCE's `_stay` at 9729-9733) break under SIG_SPACE=tokens, where ENC_SEQ and the encoder's embedding table are sized to the token vocabulary (ENC_V = V)? Byte values <256 are valid token ids, so it would not raise — it would silently encode in the wrong space — but I did not trace whether any caller guards on SIG_SPACE.

In COHERENCE's self-reference branch the centroids come from `asm.cent` (built from `_sigw`-byte reservoir windows) while `_stay` encodes WIN-byte windows of the continuation. Whether the resulting scale mismatch systematically biases the 'stay home' fraction up or down is not determinable from the source alone.

Whether `fab._sample_ord` / `fab._sample_mix` are actually left armed at the end of a real run depends on `_nbwd` modulo `MANAGE_EVERY // BATCH_W` at the final flush; I could not determine this statically for a given configuration.

`bpb_true` defaults `use_mem=True`, so NON-STATIONARY's ACTIVE/FADED figures and both UNLEARN baselines include the memory blend, while RETENTION and ACROSS THE RUN BOUNDARY's headline are weights-only. I did not find a line in the report that states this difference to the reader.

EPOCHS defaults to 1, but with EPOCHS>1 the training loop resets to the stream start each epoch, so RETENTION's 'earliest windows' are revisited at the start of every epoch and are not 'what it saw first' in training time. I did not verify whether the per-epoch reset re-splices the stream (which would also change `labels`).

`fab.grown`/`fab.removed` appear never to be restored from a checkpoint, which I inferred from the absence of any assignment other than the constructor; I did not read the full checkpoint-load block for the fabric to rule out an indirect restore.

The DID IT FIRE row `fabric.grow` reads `_fb.grown`, which is incremented by BOTH `grow()` and `spawn_from()` (self_organize.py:2005 and 2150), so `fabric.grow` and `fabric.spawn` are not disjoint counts. Whether that is intended is not stated anywhere in the audit.
